data.current_description:
Requires topics:write or a legacy key and the current Business plan.
Writes MAIN content unless branch_id explicitly selects a branch of this
topic. Main body replacement atomically advances its document revision
and collaboration epoch, records version history, updates references,
marks translated content stale, and records the receipt/webhook intent.
It refuses accepted collaborative updates that are not yet materialized.
Branch bodies have independent revisions and reference indexes; a pure
branch write leaves main body, history, translations, and webhook intent
unchanged. A mixed branch/title patch also changes shared topic metadata
and marks translations stale for that title change.
Use the strong ETag from GET as If-Match to protect both revisions, or
supply expected_document_revision/expected_metadata_revision in the body.
For branch content, use that branch's document revision and the shared
topic metadata revision. Without explicit preconditions, the handler
reads a current basis and SQL still checks it atomically against races.
Exact retries retain their original basis; they do not become new edits.
Body limits are the same as topic creation.
data.description_suggestion: Updates a topic's content, metadata, or branch. Requires `topics:write` permission and Business plan. By default, updates the main content; use `branch_id` to update a specific branch instead. Main content updates atomically advance the document revision, record version history, update references, and trigger webhooks. Branch updates have independent revisions and do not affect main content or translations. Mixed updates (branch + title) also change shared metadata and mark translations stale. Use If-Match header with the ETag from GET, or supply `expected_document_revision` and `expected_metadata_revision` in the request body for optimistic concurrency control. Request bodies follow the same 3 MiB limit as topic creation. Exact retries with the same Idempotency-Key preserve the original basis.

data.current_description:
Requires topics:write or a legacy key and the current Business plan.
Writes MAIN content unless branch_id explicitly selects a branch of this
topic. Main body replacement atomically advances its document revision
and collaboration epoch, records version history, updates references,
marks translated content stale, and records the receipt/webhook intent.
It refuses accepted collaborative updates that are not yet materialized.
Branch bodies have independent revisions and reference indexes; a pure
branch write leaves main body, history, translations, and webhook intent
unchanged. A mixed branch/title patch also changes shared topic metadata
and marks translations stale for that title change.
Use the strong ETag from GET as If-Match to protect both revisions, or
supply expected_document_revision/expected_metadata_revision in the body.
For branch content, use that branch's document revision and the shared
topic metadata revision. Without explicit preconditions, the handler
reads a current basis and SQL still checks it atomically against races.
Exact retries retain their original basis; they do not become new edits.
Body limits are the same as topic creation.

Use If-Match header with the ETag from GET, or supply `expected_document_revision` and `expected_metadata_revision` in the request body for optimistic concurrency control.
